decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: 'Flow 1 is ready... Click Save link... prefilled a sample address'; round 4 client: 'I clicked Save link, and yes — this is exactly what I was hoping for.' Round 5 gate confirms saving one valid link.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Saving a bookmark by entering a url conforms to reference; no departure to surface.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: bookmark came back 'with its title, source, and description' (later gate round 5: 'title, source, and description'). Round 4 client: 'a real title... the site it's from, and a short description.' No mention of favicon or preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires collecting title, description, favicon AND preview image. Presentation covers title/source/description only; favicon and preview image are absent. Client approved without expressing the difference — partial divergence passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker goal summary: 'a pleasant, searchable library... supports your own labels and read-later status... Is that the right direction?' (no mention of case handling). Round 2 client: 'when I search, I want it to be forgiving — finding things even if my capitalization is off.'
decisions.note: Specification framing gate. The asked-about scope omitted case-insensitivity (REF-BM-13); client requests this reference requirement, adding it to scope. Extend capture. (Later realized conformingly at round 18 — separate decision.)

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker summary treats search and labels as separate features. Round 2 client: 'letting me narrow by a label as part of searching, not just plain word matching.'
decisions.note: Specification framing gate. Client requests combining full-text search with tag filtering (reference edge rule: #-tag and full-text combine with AND; relates to REF-BM-11/REF-BM-12), missing from the presented scope. Extend capture. (Realized at round 19 — separate decision.)

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker summary covers 'read-later status' but not archiving. Round 2 client: 'beyond "read later," I'd like a way to tuck older bookmarks out of the way without deleting them, so my main list stays clean but I can still get them back later.'
decisions.note: Specification framing gate. Client extends the asked-about scope with archiving (REF-BM-26), a reference requirement absent from the maker's summary. Extend capture. (Realized at rounds 24-27 — separate decisions.)

decisions.evidence: Rounds 6-8 maker: duplicate flow stops with 'Keep as is' vs 'Update bookmark', 'without creating another copy'. Round 8 client: 'without ever making a second copy — that's exactly the duplicate handling I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Re-saving an existing url guides to editing the existing bookmark rather than duplicating — conforms to REF-BM-06.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 9-10 maker: 'the whole card should be clickable and the real page should open in a new browser tab'. Round 10 client: 'the whole card acts as the link, it opens the real page in a new tab.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Selecting a list item navigates to the original url — conforms to REF-BM-08.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 11-14 maker: optional labels at save, later labeling, and 'one bookmark may have several labels'. Round 14 client: 'keeping several labels on one bookmark — that covers how I want to organize.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Assigning one or more tags to a bookmark — conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 11-13 maker present label entry via a prefilled label field/editor ('prefilled with "learning"', sample label 'reference' added) with no autocomplete of existing tags. Round 11-14 client approves label entry ('adding a label at save time feels natural') with no mention of autocomplete/suggestions.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-10 requires offering existing tags as autocomplete on tag entry. The presented label-entry mechanism offers no autocomplete; client approves without expressing the difference. Divergence passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 15-17 maker: clicking 'learning' filter 'narrows the list down to only the two links carrying that label'; settled as sidebar. Round 17 client: 'clicking one to see only the bookmarks with that label.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Select a specific tag to filter — conforms to REF-BM-11. (Row-vs-sidebar placement at round 16 is a functionally equivalent UI preference, excluded.)

decisions.evidence: Round 18 maker: 'capitalization is ignored... partial remembered word may match either the title or description'. Round 18 client: 'Typing "INTERACTIVE"... still found the MDN bookmark even though the word only appears... in lowercase.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search realized conformingly; distinct decision/stage from the round-2 framing extend for the same requirement (counted once each).

decisions.evidence: Rounds 18-20 maker frame search as 'matching partial text in titles and descriptions'; round 20 gate: 'complete search behavior—matching partial text in titles and descriptions... combining with the selected sidebar label.' Round 20 client: 'Partial words matching in either the title or description... that's the forgiving... search I was after.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + completeness gate. REF-BM-12 requires full-text search over title, description, note AND url; the presented (and gate-declared 'complete') search covers title and description only, omitting url. Client accepts without expressing the narrower scope — divergence passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 21-23 maker: bookmark starts 'Read later', 'Mark as read' changes status; rounds 36-37: 'Mark unread' returns to 'Read later'. Round 37 client: 'move a bookmark freely between "Read later" and "Read," both ways.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Mark read-later/read and reverse — conforms to REF-BM-17/REF-BM-19. (Button-vs-checkbox at round 22 is a functionally equivalent UI preference, excluded.)

decisions.evidence: Rounds 24-27 maker: Archive removes card from main list, 'moved rather than deleted', Archive destination in sidebar, Restore preserves title/description/labels/read status with 'no duplicate'. Round 27 client: 'moving a bookmark out of the main list without deleting it... clearly distinct from deleting.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Archive hides from default list while preserving content (REF-BM-26), archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27), separate archive view (REF-BM-28) — all conform. (Button-vs-menu at round 25 is a functionally equivalent UI preference, excluded.)

decisions.evidence: Rounds 38-39 maker: re-saving an archived link recognizes it, 'create no copy', offers 'Keep archived' or 'Restore bookmark'. Round 39 client: 'making no copy, and letting me either keep it archived or restore.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + gate. Archived-duplicate handling ties duplicate convergence (REF-BM-06) to archive state — conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker lists 15 settled flows and asks 'May I start implementing this scope?' — no edit-details flow. Round 42 client: 'I'd still expect the ordinary "manage" basics to be there — being able to fix a bookmark's details if the auto-filled title is off... just don't want them to fall out of scope.' Round 43 maker: 'Editing auto-filled details... recorded for a later cycle, as agreed.'
decisions.note: Implementation-scope gate. Client surfaces editing auto-collected/bookmark details (REF-BM-03/REF-BM-04), missing from the presented scope, and requests it stay in scope (deferred to next cycle by mutual agreement). Extend capture; the round-43 deferral is the linked disposition, counted as one decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker scope list has no delete flow (only reversible archive). Round 42 client: 'to delete a link outright when I'm truly done with it (separate from archiving)... just don't want them to fall out of scope.' Round 43 maker: 'permanent deletion are recorded for a later cycle, as agreed.'
decisions.note: Implementation-scope gate. Client surfaces permanent deletion (REF-BM-05), distinct from archiving, absent from presented scope, and requests it remain in scope (deferred). Extend capture; round-43 deferral is the linked disposition.
